title: Degraded iterator mode and retry-hints for embed-ranker compatibility bridge
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Background: Multiple client SDKs (internal and third-party) rely on stable cursor semantics and predictable HTTP error surface for embeddings+rerank flows. Recent runtime improvements (continuous batching + dynamic kernel selection) introduced subtle changes to page token liveness and transient failure behavior. Problem: Legacy clients see duplicate/missing items during pagination, and callers surface opaque 5xx variants that trigger hard-fail logic rather than graceful retries. Goal: Provide a compatibility bridge that preserves iterator stability and exposes machine-readable retry hints so older clients can degrade gracefully instead of failing hard. The bridge should be lightweight, opt-in by default for legacy API keys, and fully testable in staging before rollout.
proposal: 1) Degraded iterator mode: when serving a legacy cursor, return an opaque stable cursor format that encodes: sequence checkpoint, tombstone marker list (ids removed since cursor), and TTL. The runtime will guarantee idempotent forward iteration (no skipped items) for TTL duration, tracking prefix checkpoints in the compatibility layer cache. 2) Retry-hints: map transient failures to a small structured hint sent as an HTTP header 'X-Redwood-Retry-Hint' and a JSON field in error bodies. Hints include 'backoff' (suggested ms), 'retryable' (true/false), and 'prefer-fallback' (model variant id). 3) Error-code harmonization: normalize internal transient codes to client-facing 429/503/504 categories and attach a machine-readable 'compat_code' for diagnostics. 4) Graceful fallback: when the bridge detects an unrecoverable cursor tombstone, return a 409 with a suggested canonical restart token and set 'prefer-fallback' to instruct SDKs to call fallback endpoints. 5) Metrics: add per-route counters for compat-mode hits, cursor-rewrites, and hint-consumption events.
tradeoffs: - Pros: preserves UX for older clients, reduces support load, provides actionable retry guidance. - Cons: adds compatibility-layer state (cache TTL), increases complexity in runtime routing, modest additional SLO pressure. TTL choices create a tradeoff between storage and client reliability. - Rollout risk: incorrect tombstone handling could still produce duplicates; mitigation is an initial short TTL and canary traffic split.
acceptance_criteria: - Legacy client test harness iterates a seeded dataset across 1000 pages with simulated deletes and sees no missing items when using compat cursors. - SDK integration test consumes 'X-Redwood-Retry-Hint' and follows suggested backoff successfully for transient 503s. - Metrics for compat-mode show <=1% added p95 latency at canary scale. - No increase in production duplicate-rate detected in first 48h of canary (baseline + 0.1%).
rollout_plan: 1) Implement bridge behind feature flag and enable for internal SDK keys. 2) Run compatibility tests in staging for 5 days. 3) Canary 5% of production traffic for 72 hours; monitor duplication, missing items, and error-rate dashboards. 4) Expand to 25% for 48 hours, then full rollout if metrics stable. 5) Post-rollout: 7-day observation window and support runbook distributed to SRE and Customer Support.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for cursor encoding/decoding, tombstone merge logic, and cache expiry. - Integration test: simulate interleaved writes/deletes while iterating with compat cursor. - Chaos test: inject 503/timeout and verify retry-hint consumption path in SDK integration. - Load test: ensure compat cache eviction under peak traffic behaves to SLA.
api_contract_examples: Example success: 200 OK + body { 'items': [...], 'cursor': 'rwr:ckpt=1234;ttl=1200;ts=0' } Example transient: 503 + headers { 'X-Redwood-Retry-Hint': 'retryable=true;backoff=200;prefer-fallback=model-lt-1' } Example unrecoverable cursor: 409 + body { 'error': 'cursor_expired', 'suggested_restart_token': 'rwr:restart=5678' }
observability_requirements: - Dashboard: compat-mode throughput, tombstone-rate, cursor-gen-rate, duplicate-detection-rate. - Tracing: propagate 'compat_cursor_id' and 'compat_mode' tag. - Logs: record cursor-rewrites with original and new token masked. - Alert: duplicate-rate > 0.5% for 1h or compat-mode p50 latency regression > 50ms.
decisions: - Use short-lived compat TTL default 20 minutes for initial rollout. - Surface retry hints as both header and JSON field for maximum client compatibility. - Normalize internal transient errors to 503 + 'compat_code' rather than inventing new 5xx codes.

engineering_tasks: ENG-setup-compat-cache: implement in-memory LRU with optional Redis backing
ENG-error-mapper: map internal codes to 429/503/504 and attach compat_code
ENG-sdk-integration: parse X-Redwood-Retry-Hint in Node/Python SDKs
support_runbook: - If customers report duplicates: check compat-mode logs for tombstone-merges and advise client to retry with suggested restart token. - If missing items: escalate to Eng lead with trace id and affected cursor id. - If high duplication rate: disable compat feature flag and roll back canary.
customer_impact_summary: Medium risk customers (legacy SDKs, large vector stores) may experience transient pagination anomalies. This bridge reduces support tickets by giving clients retry guidance and stable cursors for a short TTL.
